stem: Period 3 elements react with chlorine gas, $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$, to form chlorides.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The table shows the differences in observations which occur when two Period 3 chlorides are added to water.

| Period 3 chloride | observations when added to water | pH of solution formed with water |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\text{NaCl}$ | White solid disappears. Colourless solution made. | 7 |
| $\text{SiCl}_4$ | Pale yellow solution forms. Bubbles form and the test-tube feels hot. White precipitate forms. | 1-2 |

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction occurring when $\text{SiCl}_4$ is added to cold water. Include state symbols.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction occurring when $\text{SiCl}_4$ is added to water. Ignore the exothermic/endothermic nature of the reaction.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Explain, in terms of bonding, why $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{SiCl}_4$ behave differently when added to water.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: Explain, in terms of electronegativity, why the bonding in $\text{NaCl}$ is different from the bonding in $\text{SiCl}_4$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
$\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$ dissolves in cold water and reacts with it.

$$\text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{HCl} + \text{HClO}$$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Identify the oxidation number of chlorine in each of the chlorine-containing species in this reaction.

| chlorine-containing species | $\text{Cl}_2$ | $\text{HCl}$ | $\text{HClO}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| oxidation number of chlorine |  |  |  |

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction occurring.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why chlorine is used in the purification of water.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A mixture of $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HClO}$ is added to cold dilute $\text{NaOH}$. One of the products behaves as a bleach.

Suggest the equation for the reaction occurring.
